newsitem.title: CHINA: Beijing in final spruce up ahead of Hong Kong gala.
newsitem.headline: Beijing in final spruce up ahead of Hong Kong gala.

text.p: China's capital won a last-minute facelift on Friday as it prepared for gala celebrations to mark the historic return of Hong Kong only four days away.

As newly-planted flags stood atop office blocks and pennants fluttered along busy Beijing streets, an army of workmen put final touches to signboards proclaiming "Wash away 100 years of national shame" and arranged floral displays depicting the Chinese characters for "Celebrate the return of Hong Kong".
Electricians scampered up telephone poles to hang strings of electric lights and street cleaners in straw hats swept away layers of choking dust and discarded paper.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, ending 156 years of British colonial rule.
Britain wrested the territory from a weak imperial China and the handover is seen as erasing a humiliating past and confirming that China is now a modern-day political power.
Some 100,000 people are expected to gather in Tiananmen Square in the heart of Beijing to witness the historic moment, signalled on a huge countdown clock.
At zero hour a storm of fireworks will light up the capital's midnight sky and be televised live across the country.
Workmen with towels over their heads shielding them from the midday sun hammered down tacks to hold carpeting in place on a reviewing stand near Tiananmen Square.
"We have been working flat out for the last two days," said Liang Changhui of the company installing the carpeting.
"We should be ready by this evening."
Nearby, Han Chong was similarly pleased with the light fixtures placed around Tiananmen Square.
"We're almost through here," said the supervisor with the Shanghai company installing the lighting equipment.

Beijing has already resurfaced its main street, the Avenue of Eternal Peace, which passes along the edge of Communist Party headquarters of Zhongnanhai, the old imperial palace -- known as the Forbidden City -- and the massive Tiananmen Square itself.
On a somewhat smaller scale, other residents were making their own final preparations.
A young man named Liu had just hung up the Chinese flag over his tiny street stall where he sells cigarettes and cold soft drinks. "I'm excited about the return of Hong Kong," he said.

And Han Wenhu proudly displayed the flashy orange seat cover he had just bought for his pedicab. "This is new," he said, adding that perhaps it would attract a little Hong Kong handover-related business.
